questions.scenario: A company shows ৳3 crore quarterly profit but only ৳11 lakh cash. Most professional explanation:
options: One of the reports must be fraudulent
Profit is earned when promises are made (B/L date); cash arrives when promises settle — the gap sits in receivables/inventory timing
Cash is irrelevant if profit is positive
questions.explanation: Accrual profit and bank balance measure different things. Growing factories lock money INTO receivables and inventory — profitable AND cash-tight simultaneously, which is why forecasting exists.
wrongExplanations: Both can be perfectly honest — they answer different questions.
Profit is a disciplined measurement (Modules 1-8); calling it fake abandons everything this course built.
Cash pays salaries; ignoring it is how profitable factories die.

questions.scenario: Which aging bucket demands Finance + MD attention for an EXPORT receivable, and why?
options: 90+ days — collection risk AND Bangladesh Bank realization-window compliance risk converge
questions.explanation: Past 90 days you face both commercial danger (disputes hardening) and regulatory pressure (the ~120-day realization rule from Module 7). Escalation is mandatory, not optional.
wrongExplanations: Young receivables need no action yet.
Watch-list items get soft reminders only.
For exports, age IS regulation.

questions.scenario: Three-way matching before ANY supplier payment compares:
options: Purchase order vs approved GRN vs supplier invoice — price, quantity, approval all agreeing
questions.explanation: The trio proves: what we AGREED to buy (PO), what actually ARRIVED and passed QC (approved GRN), what they CLAIM (invoice). All three align → schedule payment; anything else → hold and resolve.
wrongExplanations: Bank statements show what we PAID — after the fact.
Quotations belong to procurement selection, not payment control.
Informal approvals bypass the document chain (Module 0's Golden Rule again).

questions.scenario: Supplier invoice ৳18L, GRN ৳18L approved, PO ৳17.5L. Correct handling:
options: HOLD payment; procurement resolves the ৳50k variance via approved amendment or credit note before release
Split the difference with the supplier verbally
questions.explanation: The match failed on PRICE. Until an authorized document explains the delta (PO amendment or supplier credit note), the payment calendar excludes it — protecting Masco from funding others' errors.
wrongExplanations: GRN proves quantity received, not agreed price.
Silent short-payment damages trust and creates reconciliation chaos.
Verbal agreements leave no document trail — Module 0 forbids it.

questions.scenario: Weekly forecast: opening ৳9L + collections 25L − payments 44L = negative ৳10L. Best response set:
options: Act EARLY: accelerate confirmed collections, negotiate payment scheduling, use approved credit lines — discovered Monday it's logistics, Friday it's crisis
questions.explanation: Forecasting buys TIME: options are plentiful at week-start, nearly zero at due-date. The whole discipline exists to convert crises into logistics.
wrongExplanations: Hope is not a treasury policy.
Salary delays break legal obligations and workforce trust first.
Hiding payables corrupts AP records while fixing nothing.

questions.scenario: Buyer-E's ৳12L aged 110d settles at ৳9L with ৳3L documented claim settlement. Recording requires:
options: Receipt entry for ৳9L PLUS evidence-backed settlement/write-off of ৳3L through proper approvals
questions.explanation: Money AND truth: the receipt closes part of the promise; the remainder leaves receivables only through a documented, approved loss — keeping the audit trail complete (Module 13 expands claims).
wrongExplanations: Leaving 3L open forever poisons aging forever.
Unexplained write-offs are audit findings and fraud magnets.
The sale happened; only the uncollectable portion is settled away.

options: Booking an estimated expense NOW for aged receivables unlikely to collect, based on aging percentages — honesty about probability, refined by evidence later
Refusing future orders from slow buyers
questions.explanation: Matching principle applied to promises: if aging says some won't convert, pretending otherwise overstates assets and THIS period's profit. Actual write-offs follow later WITH evidence (Module 13).
wrongExplanations: It's statistical prudence, not insult.
Credit decisions are separate commercial tools.
It's an accounting estimate, not a tax instrument.

questions.scenario: Why does RELIABLE payment behavior toward suppliers create financial value?
options: Reliability earns priority allocation, better terms, and flexibility during shortages — worth real margin points across seasons
Only banks care about payment history
questions.explanation: In RMG supply chains, trusted buyers get yarn first during crunches and gentler terms during negotiations. Payment discipline is an intangible asset with visible P&L effects.
wrongExplanations: Supplier memory is long and priced in.
Suppliers extend implicit credit exactly like banks do — with the same risk logic.
Late fees flow the other way.

questions.scenario: Nasrin asks why 'complete documents' matter so much for collections. Best answer:
options: Buyers' payment runs reject incomplete sets — missing/amended B/Ls or invoice discrepancies stall realization and push invoices into dangerous aging buckets
questions.explanation: Under LC terms especially, discrepancy = delay = aging. The cheapest collection strategy is flawless documentation at shipment time — entirely within Nasrin's control.
wrongExplanations: The paperwork exists to prove entitlement under banking rules, not for pleasure.
Documents describe goods; they never change them.
LC settlements REQUIRE compliant documents — nothing is automatic.

questions.scenario: Rafiq designs the weekly cash forecast job. Its most defensible data sources are:
options: Open AR rows with buyer payment history + AP maturity calendar + scheduled payroll/statutory dates — all from live subledgers
Last year's bank statements copied forward
questions.explanation: Forecasts inherit credibility from their inputs: live subledger balances (Module 3), behavioral patterns per buyer, contractual due dates, immovable statutory outflows. Everything else is decoration.
wrongExplanations: Intuition can supplement judgment calls, never replace ledger data.
Year-old statements miss every new promise made since.
Optimism is not data (though sales teams will offer plenty).
